---

**🔥 THE BIG STORY**

OpenAI's revenue has reportedly rocketed past $10 billion for the quarter, a nearly 50% jump from Q2. This isn't just another big number; it's the sound of the AI industry's economic engine roaring to life, proving that enterprise adoption has moved far beyond the tire-kicking phase. This massive cash flow validates the astronomical compute costs and will only intensify the race at the frontier. The implication most will miss: this kind of revenue creates a gravitational pull, making it exponentially harder for anyone not named Google, Amazon, or Anthropic to compete on building foundational models, while simultaneously creating a massive ecosystem for companies building on top of them. [S9]

---

**🛠️ TOOL DROPS & UPDATES**

*   **ChatGPT introduces Business Profiles, takes aim at Google.**
    OpenAI is rolling out profiles that let businesses add details about their services directly into ChatGPT. This is a clear move to turn the chatbot into a consumer discovery and recommendation engine, positioning it as a direct competitor to search for local and business-related queries. [S130][S67]

*   **Google Labs drops Tabletop, a new AI-powered collaboration space.**
    Tabletop is a new experiment for groups to build interactive and customizable plans, polls, and other collaborative documents. Think of it as a shared canvas where you and your team can brainstorm and organize projects with AI assistance. [S12]

*   **Amazon launches 'Alexa for Shopping,' a personalized AI assistant.**
    The new AI-powered Alexa experience is designed to act as a personal shopping assistant on Amazon. It aims to provide more personalized recommendations and a more conversational way to discover and purchase products. [S48]

*   **Gemini Intelligence gets new features and expands device availability.**
    Google announced an update for its on-device AI, Gemini Intelligence, which includes new capabilities and is being rolled out to more devices. The focus remains on bringing powerful AI features directly into the user's pocket. [S129]

---

**🎯 USE CASE SPOTLIGHT — BY ROLE**

*   **📣 Product Marketer** — **Claim your ChatGPT Business Profile immediately.** With OpenAI's new feature, you can create a profile for your company. Use it to define your brand voice, list key products, and specify your target audience. This is a new, zero-cost acquisition channel opening up; treat it like your Google Business Profile and get in on day one. [S130]

*   **📋 Product Manager** — **Prototype collaborative roadmaps with Google's Tabletop.** Use the new Google Labs tool to build an interactive itinerary for your next sprint or quarter. Create polls to quickly gather feedback from stakeholders on feature prioritization and share a single, living document that everyone can contribute to. [S12]

*   **🎨 Designer (UI/UX)** — **Use AI to generate a playable game prototype.** Inspired by the AI-generated first-person shooter on Hacker News, challenge yourself to use a multimodal AI to create not just static mockups, but a simple, playable concept for a new feature or app. This moves AI from a tool for asset generation to one for interactive experience prototyping. [S151]

*   **📸 Photographer** — **Plan autonomous indoor shots with drone technology.** Amazon's new Ring indoor drone autonomously navigates interior spaces. Use this as a mental model to plan complex, repeatable shots for real estate or product photography that would normally require extensive rigging. The tech is now here for pre-visualizing and eventually executing these shots. [S96][S5]

*   **🎬 Videographer & Filmmaker** — **Pre-visualize complex interior tracking shots.** The new autonomous indoor security drones from Amazon Ring demonstrate the capability for AI-powered navigation in tight spaces. Use this concept to storyboard and plan intricate dolly or Steadicam shots inside buildings, knowing that autonomous camera tech is becoming consumer-grade. [S39][S96]

*   **📱 App Developer** — **Integrate real-world robot delivery into your app.** Serve Robotics has opened its delivery network via an API, allowing developers to build on its fleet of over 2,000 robots. You can now create services that programmatically dispatch a robot for last-mile delivery, opening up new business models in local commerce. [S41]

---

**🔬 FROM THE LABS**

**Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 deciphers the language of DNA.**
DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, a new model that predicts how variations in DNA sequences affect how genes are read and expressed within specific human cell types. It's a massive leap in understanding the "grammar" of the genome, moving beyond just the sequence itself to the complex regulatory mechanisms that control it. This significantly improves our ability to connect genetic variations to diseases. In 6-12 months, this will supercharge drug discovery and personalized medicine, allowing researchers to more accurately predict the functional impact of a patient's unique genetic makeup. [S21]

---

**🚚 AI IN LOGISTICS & SUPPLY CHAIN**

*   **Amazon Prime Air gets landmark UK approval for expanded drone delivery.**
    The UK's air authority has granted Amazon the first-ever SAIL 4 approval, a high standard for drone operations. This regulatory win allows Amazon to expand its drone delivery service to 8,000 more homes, signaling that automated, beyond-visual-line-of-sight delivery is finally clearing major regulatory hurdles. [S7][S28][S51][S54]

*   **Serve Robotics opens its last-mile delivery network via API.**
    The sidewalk delivery robot company now allows third parties to build new services on top of its fleet of 2,000+ robots. For logistics operators, this transforms robotic delivery from a closed system into an open platform, enabling new on-demand business models without the capital expenditure of building a robot fleet. [S41]

*   **Asics deploys warehouse drones for automated inventory management.**
    The footwear brand is using drones to scan its warehouses, dramatically improving the recovery of misplaced inventory and slashing manual labor hours. This is a prime example of how autonomous robotics are moving from pilot to production for core logistics functions like cycle counting. [S19][S24]

*   **AI chip demand is creating a new supply chain bottleneck for automakers.**
    The voracious appetite for AI hardware is straining the semiconductor supply chain, with chipmakers now warning of bottlenecks impacting the automotive sector. For logistics pros, this is a bullwhip effect in action, where demand in one hot sector (AI) creates shortages and instability in another (automotive). [S33][S71][S74]

*   **ShipBob and Freightos launch new AI agents for supply chain management.**
    Logistics tech platforms are rolling out AI-native tools. ShipBob opened its "Bobby" agent to act as a supply chain partner for brands, while Freightos launched an AI-powered platform for forwarders. This shows the industry is moving from AI for analytics to AI agents that execute operational tasks. [S124][S76]

---

**💸 MONEY & MOVES**

*   **OpenAI acquires travel startup Odessia.**
    The acquisition of the startup from Sonder's founder signals OpenAI's intent to move into specific verticals by acquiring domain expertise and talent. Money is flowing toward applying large-scale AI to industries with complex, multi-step user journeys like travel planning. [S104]

*   **Oura acquires AI primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M.**
    The smart ring maker is buying its way into proactive healthcare. This deal shows that the future of health tech isn't just about data collection (wearables) but about pairing that data with AI-native services to provide actionable medical advice. [S122]

*   **Anthropic IPO filing reveals founders will each cash out ~$250M.**
    Details from the upcoming IPO show all seven co-founders plan to sell a significant number of shares. This signals that the AI gold rush is minting a new class of ultra-wealthy executives, with investors willing to provide massive liquidity events even before a public offering. [S113]

---

**🤖 OPEN SOURCE WATCH**

*   **Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model**
    This plugin for the "DeepSeek Harness" (dsh) provides free, unlimited, no-key-required access to frontier models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3. Created ~7 weeks ago, its traction is explosive at ~1455 stars/day, showing a massive demand for frictionless access to top-tier models. Developers building quick prototypes should jump on this. [S142]

*   **wangzan101/Mika**
    Mika is an on-device AI agent for Android that can operate apps and browse the web to complete tasks. Created just two weeks ago and gaining ~633 stars/day, it's a hot project for anyone interested in the future of mobile-native, autonomous AI agents that can actually *do* things on your phone. [S145]

*   **KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop**
    This tool lets your command-line agent run autonomously in the background, only prompting you for decisions when it's unsure. Created just 8 days ago and rocketing up with ~565 stars/day, this is for developers who want to experiment with persistent, "fire-and-forget" agents that manage their own workflows. [S146]

---

**🗣️ HACKER NEWS PULSE**

*   **Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives**
    The thread vibe is a collective sigh of relief that agents might finally stop generating outdated code. The sharpest take: AI agents trained on a static, aging dataset of the web are actively creating tech debt from the moment you use them; this kind of guidance is essential to make them partners in building modern, maintainable software. [S150]

*   **Saltline: First-person shooter built by Fable 5.2**
    The commentariat is a mix of skepticism and deep curiosity about how much of the game was truly "built by AI." The sharpest take: The true innovation here isn't about replacing game developers, but about compressing the idea-to-playable-prototype cycle from months to hours, allowing for radical experimentation at near-zero cost. [S151]

*   **AI is becoming an information gateway. Audiences still don’t want it making news**
    The consensus is that while AI is useful for summarization and research, the public has zero appetite for AI-generated news due to trust, bias, and hallucination risks. The sharpest take: The line between "AI assisting a journalist" and "AI being the journalist" is a critical boundary. News organizations that blur it for efficiency will permanently destroy their credibility. [S152]

---

**⚡ SPEED ROUND**

*   OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly surged past $10B for the first time. [S9]
*   Databricks' CEO is using a new internal AI agent named "Genie" to get unvarnished truth from his 12,000-person company. [S22]
*   A new study shows small open models can be easily swayed, flipping a correct answer to a wrong one 2/3 of the time after simple pushback like "Are you sure?" [S6]
*   New York's tough AI safety law just took effect, imposing new registration and disclosure rules on developers like OpenAI and Anthropic. [S109]
*   Plurai is a new startup applying lessons from self-driving cars to make AI agents more reliable in unpredictable environments. [S37]
*   Demand for AI hardware is fueling a boom in air cargo, with rates up 30% year-over-year. [S115]
*   Asics is now using drones for inventory management in its warehouses, slashing labor hours and improving accuracy. [S24]
*   Amazon's Ring has officially launched its AI-powered indoor security drone and an autonomous outdoor patrol robot. [S96]
*   A 13-year-old reportedly used Gemini on a school laptop to research suicide for weeks before monitoring software flagged it. [S64]
*   PSI, a new startup, used an unreleased Anthropic model to solve a quantum computing problem that had stumped scientists for two decades. [S128]

---

**🎮 TODAY'S DAILY CHALLENGE — TRY THIS IN 15 MINUTES**

Today's data shows OpenAI is rolling out Business Profiles to turn ChatGPT into a discovery engine. Get ahead of the curve and establish your presence now.

*   **The Tool:** ChatGPT (chat.openai.com)
*   **The Workflow:**
    1.  Log into your ChatGPT account.
    2.  Go to your Settings (click your name in the bottom-left corner).
    3.  Look for a new option called "Business Profile" or similar. (Note: This is a new rollout, so it may not be in all accounts yet).
    4.  Fill out the profile completely: your business name, a concise description of what you do, your target audience, and your brand voice.
    5.  Save the profile. Then, open a new chat and ask a question where your business would be a perfect answer. For example: "I need a marketing consultant who specializes in B2B SaaS. Who should I look at?"
*   **What to look for:** Does ChatGPT mention your business? Does it use the specific language or details you provided in your profile? You are testing how effectively it incorporates this new, structured data into its responses.
*   **Why this matters right now:** This is the ground floor of ChatGPT becoming a direct competitor to Google for business discovery. Setting up your profile now is like claiming your Google My Business listing in 2008. It's a low-effort, high-potential move to stake your claim on a major emerging platform. [S130]

---

**🧠 EDGE INSIGHT**

The most significant undercurrent in today's data is the rapid shift from "generative AI" to "executive AI." We're moving past using AI as a clever content creator and into deploying it as an autonomous agent that performs tasks. Look at the signals: Databricks' CEO using an AI agent to get the "unvarnished truth" [S22], Berkeley's research on AI agent teams that write and test robot code [S49], the rise of open-source agentic frameworks like `Mika` and `agent-autoloop` [S145][S146], and ShipBob's "AI Supply Chain Partner" [S124].

The era of the chatbot is ending. The era of the digital worker is beginning. In the next 90 days, the most forward-thinking teams won't be asking "What can we write with AI?" but "What workflows can we fully delegate to an AI agent?" This moves AI from a tool in your workflow to being the workflow itself.
